subject: Request: one-time credit + temporary tier for unexpected POC overrun (Novapulse)
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@novapulse.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Spike in usage during pilot — possible credit?

Karthik,

Quick note from the Novapulse pilot lead: we hit a much larger-than-expected burst during integration testing this morning when the new data pipeline replayed several days of traffic. Token consumption spiked ~6x for a 3-hour window. Our team is happy with latency and results, but the bill impact for the pilot month will put us over budget.

Can Redwood provide a one-time credit or a short-term tier adjustment while we stabilize the pipeline? We're still committed to the POC and intend to move to a paid pilot for July, but this sudden overrun was unplanned.

Happy to hop on a call if that helps.

Best,
Elaine Park
Director, Platform Partnerships
Novapulse, Inc.
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Spike in usage during pilot — possible credit?
Attachments: novapulse_q2_usage_snapshot.csv (csv), karthik_proposed_credit_memo.pdf (pdf)

Team — forwarding an ask from Novapulse. TL;DR: unexpected 6x token spike for ~3 hours during a data replay. They want a one-time credit or a temporary tier while they stabilize.

My suggested options (cheap to Redwood but saves the deal):
- Option A (preferred): one-time credit of up to $15,000 to wipe the overage, plus a temporary 10% discount on token rates for the remainder of pilot month (2 weeks). Requires sign-off from Marissa/Finance.
- Option B: convert the pilot to a short-term committed tier: 1 month at reduced rate if they commit to a 6-month minimum starting July (reduces immediate revenue impact).
- Option C: give a bill smoothing credit equal to 50% of the overage and offer faster onboarding support to avoid repeats.

Attached is a usage snapshot and a short memo with calculation details. This account is a high-velocity enterprise target; losing momentum here will make it harder to convert. They indicated willingness to sign an amendment if we offer relief.

Ask: Marissa/Ben — can we approve Option A or is there a preferred path from finance? If finance wants a cap or coupling to a commitment, I can propose the amendment language and loop legal.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike in usage during pilot — possible credit?

Karthik — thanks for the context and the proposed options. A couple of follow-ups before we commit cash:

1) Ben, please confirm the exact gross margin impact for a $15k one-time credit vs a 10% temporary discount for 2 weeks on their projected pilot spend. We need to quantify the net revenue delta and any downstream ARR tradeoffs.

2) Karthik: can you confirm Novapulse's willingness to sign a short amendment that either (a) consents to a 6-month minimum starting July, or (b) agrees to a follow-on committed pilot? If they will not sign, we should limit the credit.

3) Also, is this a one-off caused by their pipeline replay, or a pattern we should flag (do they have a streaming/ingest cadence that could repeat)? If there's recurrence risk, we should require a commit.

If Ben's numbers look acceptable and Karthik can get a signed amendment, I'm inclined to approve a capped credit with the discount conditionally applied.

— Marcus
VP, Sales Operations
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-21T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike in usage during pilot — possible credit? (finance view)

Marcus / Team,

I ran the numbers against the usage snapshot. Key points:
- Estimated overage for the spike window: $22,800 (per the CSV).
- Option A (one-time credit $15k + 10% temp discount): net immediate hit ~ $13,500 to gross margin after cost-of-serving adjustments.
- Option B (commitment swap): converts $22.8k of spend into booked committed revenue if they sign a 6-month minimum at a slightly reduced rate; modeled NPV is neutral-positive compared to write-off, but requires legal amendment and longer sales cycle to finalize.

Recommendation: approve a capped one-time customer credit of up to $15,000 contingent on: (1) a signed amendment within 7 business days that either (a) commits to a 6-month minimum or (b) converts the pilot into a paid committed pilot starting July, and (2) a written confirmation from Novapulse that the spike was non-recurring (ops note). If the amendment is not signed in the window, we roll back the temporary discount and only apply a reduced credit (max $5k).

Marissa: if you approve the contingency path above, I will draft the finance memo and credit authorization for accounting to process.

Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Finance
Redwood Inference

On Tue, Jun 20, 2027 at 11:03 AM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Karthik — thanks for the context and the proposed options....
>
summary: Novapulse experienced an unplanned usage spike. AE recommended a one-time credit plus short discount to preserve momentum. Finance recommends approving up to $15k contingent on signed amendment (6-month minimum or paid pilot) and ops confirmation. Final approval requested from Marissa for VP/CFO sign-off.
note_for_inbox: This thread lives in the 'Inbox' folder for karthik_iyer; it contains internal escalation to get VP/CFO sign-off for a customer credit tied to a pilot overrun.
